correctness.rationale: For n attributes and m distinct records, the C(n,2) attribute pairs demand distinct row-pair witnesses: C(m,2)>=C(n,2), hence m>=n. At equality, all row pairs witness exactly one attribute pair, forcing partition-mask intersections exactly one and row-edge multiplicity two. Enumerating all canonical partitions into at most three groups and all increasing-index families with row-edge multiplicity <=2 is exhaustive. At m=3,5,6 there are 4,40,121 column masks, and zero complete m-element families in both standalone algorithms. Direct verification checks the explicit 4x4,6x5,7x7 witnesses and projected 4x3 and 7x6 tables. The known theorem f(3,3)=7 excludes n>=8. The computation is finite and the reduction, not the terminal log alone, proves exhaustiveness.

originality.rationale: The two strict boundary values mu(5)=6 and mu(6)=7 and the resulting complete ternary three-key minimum-row spectrum are not entailed by prior existence of 7x7 codes, by maximal-column bounds f(3,3)=7, nor by the generic m>=n counting inequality. Relevant earlier works were compared at the level of these statements and their implications, including the 1984 treatment of minimum Armstrong relation size. Unindexed computation remains possible.
residual_risks: A specialist unpublished or poorly indexed exhaustive study could independently obtain the n=5 and n=6 record minima.
The full 1995 orthogonal-double-cover article was not available for a complete comparison; abstract concerns a broader graph class and does not decide this ternary partition problem.
Only particular sections/pages of the 1994 ODC paper were inspected; unreviewed pages are not asserted to be unrelated.
The 1984 bibliographic date is journal metadata without a confirmed first public release day; 1994-06-30 is used as the earliest independently verified day-level public-source anchor.

value.rationale: The least number of database tuples needed to realize exactly the triples as minimal keys is a natural quantitative invariant under a fixed small domain size. A complete all-admissible-length profile determines exact storage/test-case minima, with two strict gaps relative to the natural pair-counting floor and explicit witnesses. Neither mere correctness nor code generation is being substituted for this intrinsic motivation. The result is finite but solves the whole q=3,k=3 row-minimum function because the known length bound cuts off at n=7.
